newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: At least 225 killed in Sri Lankan rebel attacks.
newsitem.headline: At least 225 killed in Sri Lankan rebel attacks.

text.p: At least 65 Sri Lankan soldiers and policemen and 160 Tamil rebels were killed when Tamil Tiger rebels on Thursday attacked two bases and shelled a town in the island's east, military officials said on Friday.

In the bigger of the two pre-dawn attacks, about 800 guerrillas belonging to the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) overran Vaunathivu camp in Batticaloa, about 200 km (125 miles) from the capital Colombo. The camp was later retaken by government forces.

"Some of those killed are soldiers and policemen who were guarding Batticaloa town when the rebels fired mortars at the town," a military official in the east told Reuters in providing latest casualty reports.

The LTTE is fighting for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in this predominantly Sinhalese Indian Ocean island's north and east in a 14-year civil war in which at least 50,000 people have died.
Military officials said at least 50 of the camp's 200-plus soldiers were killed and 70 wounded in the attack on the Vaunathivu camp.
"Ground troops monitoring LTTE radio transmissions say at least 160 of their men had been killed," a spokesman said.
One soldier also died in a rebel attack on the China Bay air force base in eastern Trincomalee district, about 240 km (150 miles) from Colombo.
The rebels took many casualties in the three-hour attack, which began at about 11:30 p.m. (1730 GMT) on Wednesday, the spokesman said. He said no exact figures were available.
The LTTE were not immediately available for comment.
But an LTTE spokesman from London on Thursday denied the rebels suffered heavy casualties, saying the Sri Lankan government "routinely exaggerates LTTE losses and deliberately hides its own".
